summary: Confirmed DONE. The cost and both bugs from the finding are gone. Every current client (web, desktop through web, mobile) asks for threadPriorities:"delta". A ranking now sends those clients one small thread-priorities item, read once per server and shared by all subscribers. The client patches only the summaries whose priority changed. Older clients still get a full snapshot, but the read is shared (single-flight plus coalesceConcurrentRuns). getThreadShellById includes the projected priority, so an upsert no longer erases it. The snapshot updatedAt includes rankedAt, so a re-rank at an unchanged sequence counts as 'newer'. I found no other caller that turns a ranking into a full snapshot. The CLI remote takes only the first snapshot. ensureCurrent callers do not refetch the shell. Expired rankings are filtered on the client by isUsableThreadPriorityRanking. Only a minor ordering race remains, and I traced its actual mechanism (see fixDefects).

evidence.note: priorityStream: a delta client gets {kind:'thread-priorities', priorities} from listThreadPriorities. Any other client gets a fallback snapshot. Both reads go through joinPriorityLoad.
joinPriorityLoad single-flight. It lives in a module-level WeakMap keyed by the shared projectionSnapshotQuery, so subscribers on different connections join the same load.
A resumed delta client gets the current rankings right after the resumed marker. Priority items are merged in only after the head snapshot or resumed items.

coordinator.changes is wired once into makeOrchestrationStreamHelpers. subscribeShell (orchestrationRpc.ts:518-548) is the only production user of makeReplayableShellStream, and it is unscoped, so the unscoped listThreadPriorities leaks nothing.
replace() deletes every ranking and the single batch slot before inserting. So 'every currently usable ranking' is exactly the latest batch, as the proposal asked.
getThreadShellById reads listThreadPriorityRows(threadId), a PK lookup on thread_priority_rankings.thread_id (migration 053), and attaches priority. The upsert-erases-priority bug is fixed.

The snapshot updatedAt takes maxIso over ranking rankedAt. Because classifyProjectionSnapshot compares sequence first and then updatedAt (projectionTracker.ts:8-29), a re-rank snapshot is now classified 'newer'.
getShellSnapshot outside transactions goes through coalesceConcurrentRuns, so the fallback snapshot path is shared too.

Routes thread-priorities to applyThreadPriorities and asks for delta whenever the host supplies the callback. Web wires it at apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:888, mobile at apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:514.
Priority items share the shell batcher (FIFO with upserts, one store commit) and skip the sequence check.

applyThreadPriorities replaces priority only on changed summaries. Unchanged rows keep their identity, and it is a no-op when nothing changed. Priority lives only on SidebarThreadSummary (types.ts:275), and the only reader is threadInbox.ts:572.
The shared (threadId, sequence) read cache with a 2 s TTL is how a pre-ranking upsert can reach a second subscriber after its thread-priorities item (see fixDefects).

Tests cover the shared snapshot load, a reload for a ranking heard after the read began, the delta from one shared load, resumed rankings, and failed ranking reads on resume. Also ProjectionSnapshotQuery.test.ts:2674 (priority on upsert plus updatedAt=rankedAt) and store.test.ts:2661.

fixDefects: Minor, low impact: a thread upsert can still briefly revert a fresh ranking on the client. The delta item has no sequence, so the auditor flagged this ordering issue in general terms. I traced the actual mechanism. For a single subscriber the race is effectively closed. getThreadShellById's queries run sequentially on the one connection, so the priority read lands either before or after the ranking transaction. A pre-commit upsert is also offered to the merge before the post-commit priorities load finishes. The real window is readSharedThreadShell (apps/server/src/ws/context/sharedThreadShellReads.ts:42-75). Its (threadId, sequence) entries live for 2 s. Suppose subscriber A read a thread's shell just before a ranking committed. A slower or backpressured subscriber B (hosted relay, mobile) that maps the same event up to 2 s later gets the pre-ranking priority from the cache, possibly after B already received the thread-priorities item. That thread then shows its old or no priority until its next upsert or the next actual ranking. A cache-hit ensureCurrent publishes nothing. The impact is small: AI Focus is opt-in, a ranking takes seconds of LLM time, and active threads re-upsert quickly. A small correction to the auditor: the remark that the item carries 'every usable ranking rather than only the latest batch' is moot. replace() wipes all rankings, so the two sets are the same.
implementationSketch: Optional hardening for the race, effort S. (1) In apps/server/src/ws/context/sharedThreadShellReads.ts export invalidateSharedThreadShellReads(query: object), which clears tables.get(query). Alternatively, add a priority generation to the cache key. (2) Call it as soon as a ranking commits. The cleanest place is a single fiber in apps/server/src/ws/context.ts (next to makeOrchestrationStreamHelpers at ~1262) that runs coordinator.changes and invalidates for projectionSnapshotQuery. Another option is a Stream.tap in priorityStream (orchestrationStreams.ts:761) ahead of the joinPriorityLoad mapEffect. For a fully closed window, have ThreadPriorityCoordinator expose a generation counter bumped right after repository.replace and inside the lock, and include it in the readSharedThreadShell key. (3) Tests: in sharedThreadShellReads.test.ts, a read after invalidation queries again. In orchestrationStreamBatching.test.ts, two shell subscribers where the first caches a pre-ranking upsert, a ranking is then published, and the second subscriber's upsert of the same event carries the new priority.
